## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.

##Functions
Enter names of functions here and info what they do, theur arguments, etc.
-filter
-ggplot
-range() returns the minimum and maximum value of a vector.
-mutate() adds a new column or modifies an existing column in a data frame.
-ifelse() returns one value if a condition is TRUE, another if FALSE
-group_by() splits your data into separate groups based on a column's values, so that any calculation you do afterward (like summarize()) is done separately for each group, instead of on the whole dataset at once.

##Operators
- $ extracts a specific column by name, e.g. nettle$Langs.
- %in% checks whether each value in a vector matches any value in a given set; returns TRUE/FALSE.
- %>% the pipe operator; passes the result on its left as the first argument into the function on its right.
- <- assignment operator; stores a value/result into a named object.
